info.title: Micropod API · CacheService
info.description:
## micropod.v1.CacheService

The hvf machine's dependency caches: the units the guest engine keeps per
 scope and tool, the policy it attaches them by, and bounded pruning. Every
 call reads the live guest (its Docker socket) or the machine's own
 machine.json; nothing is cached by the API. The REST routes under
 /v1/caches answer the same data from the same code.

 Errors: `failed_precondition` while the machine is not running (no guest
 to ask) or `machine install` runs; `invalid_argument` for a request the
 REST twin would answer 400; `not_found` for an unknown container.

post.description:
Which caches attached to a container, or were skipped and why
 (GET /v1/caches/explain/{id}).

The policy in force (GET /v1/caches/policy): machine.json's `cache`
 section with defaults filled in.

The guest's cache inventory (GET /v1/caches): policy and digest, scopes,
 per-unit sizes and lock state, totals, budget, evictions and the cache
 disk.
The cache units, filtered by scope, layer and tool kind.

Lock-safe bounded eviction (POST /v1/caches/prune). A dry run unless
 `apply` is true; an apply that selects nothing also needs `all`.

Patch the policy and hot-apply it to a running guest
 (PUT /v1/caches/policy). Only the fields set change; a request that
 sets none is `invalid_argument` and writes nothing.

connect-protocol-version.title: Connect-Protocol-Version
connect-protocol-version.description: Define the version of the Connect protocol

code.description: The status code, which should be an enum value of [google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description: A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the [google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized by the client.

details.description: A list of messages that carry the error details. There is no limit on the number of messages.

type.description: A URL that acts as a globally unique identifier for the type of the serialized message. For example: `type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo`. This is used to determine the schema of the data in the `value` field and is the discriminator for the `debug` field.

value.description: The Protobuf message, serialized as bytes and base64-encoded. The specific message type is identified by the `type` field.

debug.title: Debug
debug.description: Deserialized error detail payload. The 'type' field indicates the schema. This field is for easier debugging and should not be relied upon for application logic.

connect.error_details.Any.description: Contains an arbitrary serialized message along with a @type that describes the type of the serialized message, with an additional debug field for ConnectRPC error details.

values.title: values
values.description: Repeated field of dynamically typed values.

google.protobuf.ListValue.title: ListValue
google.protobuf.ListValue.description:
`ListValue` is a wrapper around a repeated field of values.

 The JSON representation for `ListValue` is JSON array.

google.protobuf.NullValue.title: NullValue
google.protobuf.NullValue.description:
`NullValue` is a singleton enumeration to represent the null value for the
 `Value` type union.

 The JSON representation for `NullValue` is JSON `null`.

google.protobuf.Struct.description:
`Struct` represents a structured data value, consisting of fields
 which map to dynamically typed values. In some languages, `Struct`
 might be supported by a native representation. For example, in
 scripting languages like JS a struct is represented as an
 object. The details of that representation are described together
 with the proto support for the language.

 The JSON representation for `Struct` is JSON object.

google.protobuf.Value.description:
`Value` represents a dynamically typed value which can be either
 null, a number, a string, a boolean, a recursive struct value, or a
 list of values. A producer of value is expected to set one of these
 variants. Absence of any variant indicates an error.

 The JSON representation for `Value` is JSON value.

extra.title: extra
extra.description: Keys this server does not know, passed through unchanged.

micropod.v1.CacheBuildKit.title: CacheBuildKit
micropod.v1.CacheBuildKit.description: BuildKit settings in the cache policy.

state.title: state
state.description: Guest init's outcome: mounted, unavailable or none.

micropod.v1.CacheDisk.title: CacheDisk
micropod.v1.CacheDisk.description: The persistent cache disk (caches.ext4) as the guest sees it.

tools.title: tools
tools.description: Kinds or groups (go = gomod + gobuild) as configured.

defaultTrust.title: default_trust
defaultTrust.description: trusted or untrusted; unset is trusted.

extra.title: extra
extra.description:
Keys this server does not know, kept in machine.json and passed to the
 guest unchanged.

micropod.v1.CachePolicy.title: CachePolicy
micropod.v1.CachePolicy.description:
machine.json's `cache` section, as the guest applies it. Fields named
 optional are unset when the setting is off or cleared.

micropod.v1.CacheScopeUnits.title: CacheScopeUnits
micropod.v1.CacheScopeUnits.description: The unit names one scope holds.

discardedAtStart.title: discarded_at_start
discardedAtStart.description:
Units (scope/unit) moved to trash at the engine's start because an
 unclean stop left them marked dirty.

keptAtStart.title: kept_at_start
keptAtStart.description: Marked units kept at the engine's start (their boot stopped cleanly).

unavailable.title: unavailable
unavailable.description: Why the guest has no shared caches this boot; unset while they work.

micropod.v1.CacheStringList.title: CacheStringList
micropod.v1.CacheStringList.description: A list that can be set to empty, which an absent list cannot say.

inUse.title: in_use
inUse.description: A container holds the unit's lock.

dirty.title: dirty
dirty.description:
The crash fence has the unit marked dirty: prune and the janitor leave
 it alone. Absent from guests that predate the fence.

micropod.v1.CacheUnit.title: CacheUnit
micropod.v1.CacheUnit.description: One unit: a tool's store in one scope.

cache.title: cache
cache.description: Absent when the guest recorded no plan.

micropod.v1.ContainerCacheExplain.title: ContainerCacheExplain
micropod.v1.ContainerCacheExplain.description: Explain: the cache plan the guest recorded when it created the container.

trust.title: trust
trust.description: untrusted or readonly; unset is trusted.

proxy.title: proxy
proxy.description: The dependency proxy decision per tool kind.

toolsReported.title: tools_reported
toolsReported.description: True when the guest sent a `tools` map (possibly empty).

proxyReported.title: proxy_reported
proxyReported.description: True when the guest sent a `proxy` map (possibly empty).

access.title: access
access.description: copy-on-write or read-only; unset is the store itself.

id.title: id
id.description: Container ID — `container` uses the user-assigned name as the ID.

micropod.v1.ContainerRef.title: ContainerRef
micropod.v1.ContainerRef.description: Reference to an existing container (or the ID returned by run/create).

micropod.v1.Empty.title: Empty
micropod.v1.Empty.description:
The Micropod daemon API is grouped into per-domain services, one per file:

   container.proto — ContainerService (lifecycle, logs, stats, exec)
   image.proto     — ImageService (list, pull, delete)
   volume.proto    — VolumeService (volumes + mount policy)
   network.proto   — NetworkService
   compose.proto   — Compose (up/down over a compose spec)
   system.proto    — SystemService (snapshot, usage, app updates)

 Empty is shared by every service, so it lives here.

includeStats.title: include_stats
includeStats.description:
Per-unit sizes, totals and budget utilisation. Absent means true (what
 GET /v1/caches does); false is `?stats=0`, a cheaper read.

tool.title: tool
tool.description: Only this tool: a kind (gomod, npm, ...) or a group (go).

policyDigest.title: policy_digest
policyDigest.description: The digest of the policy the guest attached them by.

apply.title: apply
apply.description:
Evict for real. The default (false) is a dry run that reports what would
 be freed; there is deliberately no `dry_run` field whose default evicts.

all.title: all
all.description:
Confirm an apply that names no scope, tool, max_bytes or
 older_than_secs: every idle unit in every scope.

olderThanSecs.title: older_than_secs
olderThanSecs.description: Evict units idle longer than this; must be positive.

maxBytes.title: max_bytes
maxBytes.description:
Evict least recently used units until the total is at most this; must
 be positive.

partialGoBuild.title: partial_go_build
partialGoBuild.description: Evict old Go build-cache files instead of whole units.

micropod.v1.SetCachePolicyRequest.title: SetCachePolicyRequest
micropod.v1.SetCachePolicyRequest.description:
Every field is a change when set. "" clears go_proxy and npm_registry; 0
 clears max_bytes, max_age_days and min_free_bytes (as null does in PUT
 /v1/caches/policy).

warnings.title: warnings
warnings.description:
A policy URL opens no host port, or names one the running machine has
 not opened (it takes effect at the next start).
